summary: This is a Hurl script that automates a two-step process: first it logs into an API to get an access token, then it uses that token to download a product catalog with specific fields, saves it to a file, and validates that the data looks reasonable (more than 100 products, all have titles, all have positive prices).

explanations.7: The double curly braces {{username}} mean this is a placeholder that Hurl will replace with an actual value from your environment or variables file at runtime.
explanations.12: This line extracts the access token from the login response using a JSONPath expression and stores it in a variable named 'token' so we can use it in the next request.
explanations.16: We're using the token we captured earlier as a Bearer token in the Authorization header, which is the standard way to authenticate subsequent requests.
explanations.18: The 'limit: 0' query parameter is telling the server we want all products (0 means unlimited), rather than the default page size.
explanations.21: The 'output' option saves the response body to a file named 'products.json' on disk.
explanations.24: This assertion checks that the products array has more than 100 items; if it doesn't, the test fails.
explanations.25: This assertion verifies that every product has a title field populated; the [?!@.title] syntax finds any products missing a title.
explanations.26: This assertion ensures no products have a price of zero or negative, which would be data quality issues.
